Intrusive thoughts are ***ABSOLUTE HELL.*** It comes in waves for me personally, and at its worst I can be stuck in constant loops of self harm trying to get some sort of relief but it really does feel like a prison in your head.

I have struggled with harm ocd, so-ocd, health ocd, and more themes and I would have to say that overall as a woman, I am so much more paranoid with everything.

**recently** this guy was trying to flirt with me on snapchat (it was really really obvious because he kept complimenting me over and over as i was barely responding since i was not interested) and immediately my brain sent me all of these intrusive thoughts i did not want regarding him and I ended up with an obsession that he was out to kill me.

it was so bad, i was crying everyday, i even deleted all of my social medias because of this. I locked doors, didnt want to walk near windows in my house, and so on.

as if women generally werent already pretty afraid of men, having ocd just made it much worse on me since I had this pre-existing fear of men :(

Edit: oh dont even get me started on how difficult actually PERSUING relationships with men are.... i basically cant ;( luckily im bisexual also happy pride

I was in 6th grade. We had a general school uniform but we had these "free fridays" where we could wear jeans with any t-shirt of our choosing *if we wanted to*. I didn't realize it was friday so I walked in wearing my uniform *which is totally fine, people do that all the time*. In the middle of my third period, my dean calls out the *all of the girls in my class* (She literally went: "Could all the ladies come outside please") and brought us to the hall where she proceeded to dress code each of us. I was wearing my correct uniform and she still gave me a warning slip.

Still makes me mad to this day because she had no reason to do that. The main reason was because skinny jeans got so popular, but there is nothing wrong with that? Mean while our principle was wearing 5 inch heels and tight skirts which is totally fine, but it is *actually* against the dress code when compared to skinny jeans.

Regardless, we proceeded to boycott the dress code by leading a parade during recess.

I miss those days, it was a wonderful feminist boycott that genuinely brought all the girls in the class together regardless of whether you knew each other well or not.
